question.prompt:
Right \(\triangle ABC\) has \(AB=3,\) \(BC=4,\) and \(AC=5.\) Square \(XYZW\) is inscribed in \(\triangle ABC\) with \(X\) and \(Y\) on \(\overline{AC},\) \(W\) on \(\overline{AB},\) and \(Z\) on \(\overline{BC}.\) What is the side length of the square?

[Figure 1](figures/2007_AMC_10B_Q21_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The square's opposite sides are parallel, so \(WZ\parallel XY\parallel AC\). Therefore \(\triangle BWZ\) is similar to \(\triangle BAC\) by AA. Comparing their bases and corresponding altitudes will connect the square's side length to the triangle's dimensions.

Let \(s>0\) be the square's side length, and let \(h\) be the altitude from \(B\) to \(AC\). Since \(AC\) is the longest side of the given right triangle, the right angle is at \(B\). Computing the triangle's area in two ways gives
\[
\frac12\cdot3\cdot4=\frac12\cdot5h,
\qquad h=\frac{12}{5}.
\]
The perpendicular distance between \(AC\) and \(WZ\) is \(WX=s\). Thus the altitude of \(\triangle BWZ\) to \(WZ\) is \(h-s\), where \(0<s<h\).

Corresponding bases and altitudes in similar triangles have the same ratio, so
\[
\frac{s}{5}=\frac{h-s}{h}.
\]
Substituting \(h=\frac{12}{5}\) and multiplying by the positive denominators yields
\[
12s=60-25s,
\qquad 37s=60,
\qquad s=\frac{60}{37}.
\]
This unique solution satisfies \(0<s<\frac{12}{5}\). The square's side length is \(\boxed{\frac{60}{37}}\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Compare bases and altitudes
